scope: Introductory research classifications; does not grant model approval or planning certification

neoclassical.label: Neoclassical
neoclassical.description: Symmetry, classical columns, ordered proportions and restrained geometric composition.
neoclassical.designIdea: Clarity, order and continuity with antiquity; often used to project institutional permanence.

brutalism.label: Brutalism
brutalism.description: Expressive mass, deep openings and an overt presentation of materials, structure and construction.
brutalism.designIdea: Material directness and a serious, legible architectural presence.

modernism.label: Modernism
modernism.description: Unornamented volumes, structural grids and extensive glazing.

contemporary.label: Contemporary
contemporary.description: Current architectural vocabulary; specific examples differ in materials, roofs and composition.
contemporary.designIdea: Discuss each design’s stated aims rather than assigning one shared ideology.

minimalism.label: Minimalist contemporary
minimalism.description: Reduced material palette, plain volumes and carefully placed openings.
minimalism.designIdea: Restraint, spatial clarity and emphasis on proportion.

timber_contemporary.label: Contemporary timber
timber_contemporary.description: Visible timber frames, timber surfaces or a timber-led architectural composition.
timber_contemporary.designIdea: Making construction legible and exploring material warmth.

nordic.label: Nordic-inspired contemporary
nordic.description: In these catalogue examples: restrained palettes, timber and clear roof forms.
nordic.designIdea: Use the examples to discuss domestic scale, light and material restraint.

biophilic.label: Biophilic design
biophilic.description: Deliberate connections to planting, daylight, natural materials and natural forms.
biophilic.designIdea: Strengthening people’s connection with nature in the built environment.

gothic.label: Gothic Revival
gothic.description: Pointed openings, tracery, steep roofs and vertical accents.
gothic.designIdea: Historical continuity and expressive craftsmanship; often spiritual or collegiate associations.

italianate.label: Italianate
italianate.description: Bracketed cornices, arched openings and layered facade composition.
italianate.designIdea: Civic or commercial dignity and an urban facade addressing the street.

georgian.label: Georgian
georgian.description: Balanced facades, regularly arranged windows and a composed entrance.
georgian.designIdea: Proportion, symmetry and an orderly domestic or civic presence.

second_empire.label: Second Empire influence
second_empire.description: Mansard roofs, dormers and an elaborate roof silhouette.

belle_epoque.label: Belle Époque eclectic
belle_epoque.description: Richly articulated classical composition combined with iron, glass and other decorative vocabularies.

modernisme.label: Catalan Modernisme
modernisme.description: Decorative ironwork, coloured glass and expressive craft in these market references.
modernisme.designIdea: Integration of architecture, craft and regional cultural expression.

art_deco.label: Art Deco
art_deco.description: Geometric ornament, strong vertical accents and stepped composition.
art_deco.designIdea: Modernity expressed through decoration, craft and visual energy.

moderne.label: Streamline Moderne
moderne.description: Rounded corners, smooth surfaces and strong horizontal bands.

baronial.label: Scottish Baronial
baronial.description: Turrets, crow-stepped gables and a castle-like roofline.
baronial.designIdea: Romantic historical identity and a picturesque silhouette.

craftsman.label: Craftsman / Arts and Crafts
craftsman.description: Expressed carpentry, substantial porch elements and legible construction.
craftsman.designIdea: Craftsmanship, material care and a response to industrial standardisation.

edwardian.label: Edwardian Foursquare
edwardian.description: In this example: square massing, a hipped roof, dormer and columned porch.
edwardian.designIdea: An orderly domestic composition with restrained traditional detail.

vernacular.label: Regional vernacular
vernacular.description: Established local patterns of roofs, materials, entrances and adaptation.
vernacular.designIdea: Everyday usefulness and continuity of local building knowledge.

machiya.label: Traditional Japanese machiya
machiya.description: Timber construction, street-facing lattice and a relationship to interior gardens.
machiya.designIdea: Continuity of living, work, craft and local urban culture.

mediterranean.label: Mediterranean-inspired
mediterranean.description: For these models: arcades, stucco or stone, tiled roofs and sheltered outdoor rooms.
mediterranean.designIdea: Shaded thresholds and relationships between indoor and outdoor life.

ranch.label: Post-war Ranch
ranch.description: Low horizontal composition, broad roof and an informal street-facing domestic presence.
ranch.designIdea: Ground-oriented living and a close relationship to the private plot.

industrial.label: Industrial / utilitarian
industrial.description: Simple enclosures, working doors, repetitive bays and visible construction systems.
industrial.designIdea: Efficient accommodation of work, storage and servicing.

historic_industrial.label: Historic industrial
historic_industrial.description: Iron or steel frames, large spans, daylight glazing and brick enclosures.
historic_industrial.designIdea: Structure and daylight organised around working or public interior space.

structural.label: Expressed structure
structural.description: Exposed frames, bracing, cables or other structure as a main part of the composition.
structural.designIdea: Making the way a building or bridge stands up visually legible.

rustic.label: Rustic / Parkitecture
rustic.description: Logs, stone and crafted shelter forms that relate to a landscape setting.
rustic.designIdea: Blending built structures with their landscape.

traditional_inspired.label: Traditional-inspired contemporary
traditional_inspired.description: Current buildings using familiar pitched roofs, porches and domestic proportions.
traditional_inspired.designIdea: Familiarity and continuity of domestic form.

classical_uncertain.label: Classical / eclectic — review needed
classical_uncertain.description: A formal facade, dome or classical motif appears in the reviewed reference.
classical_uncertain.designIdea: Potential teaching themes: proportion and institutional presence.

contemporary_landscape.label: Contemporary public-space design
contemporary_landscape.description: Current arrangements of paving, seating, planting and public activity.
contemporary_landscape.designIdea: Discuss the actual arrangement, use and experience of each space.

naturalistic.label: Naturalistic / picturesque-inspired landscape
naturalistic.description: Informal planting, varied views and paths composed around landscape scenery.
naturalistic.designIdea: Restoration, discovery and attention to site character.

formal_garden.label: Formal / gardenesque tradition
formal_garden.description: Ordered beds, designed paths, garden structures or deliberately displayed planting.
formal_garden.designIdea: Cultivated display and a composed visitor experience.

japanese_garden.label: Japanese-inspired garden
japanese_garden.description: This reference combines a stream, stones, bridge and carefully framed planted views.
japanese_garden.designIdea: Attention to sequence, detail and relationships among water, stones and planting.

ecological_landscape.label: Ecological / green-infrastructure landscape
ecological_landscape.description: Wetland planting, rain gardens or other designed relationships to water and habitat.
ecological_landscape.designIdea: Connecting public landscape with environmental processes.

productive.label: Productive / community-growing landscape
productive.description: Fruit trees, allotments or demonstration planting organised for growing and learning.
productive.designIdea: Stewardship, cultivation and opportunities for shared learning.

recreation.label: Sport / recreation design — no specific style
recreation.description: Courts, play or activity equipment and their supporting outdoor space.
recreation.designIdea: Opportunities for recreation and social activity.

heritage_street.label: Traditional / historic streetscape
heritage_street.description: A fine-grained street frontage, traditional paving or a locally distinctive street pattern.
heritage_street.designIdea: Continuity of urban character and street-based daily life.

haussmann.label: Haussmannian boulevard tradition
haussmann.description: Broad tree-lined boulevards and a coordinated metropolitan street composition.
haussmann.designIdea: Movement, infrastructure and a strong metropolitan image.

canal.label: Canal-city streetscape tradition
canal.description: Waterways, narrow urban edges, planted quays and bridge crossings.
canal.designIdea: Connections among water, movement and the urban edge.

contemporary_street.label: Contemporary street / public-realm design
contemporary_street.description: Current street arrangements with deliberate allocation of movement, planting and social space.
contemporary_street.designIdea: Make the priorities visible by comparing the actual allocation of space.

engineering.label: Engineering / standard-section design
engineering.description: A prescribed road section, bridge structure or infrastructure component.

surface.label: Path / surface component — style neutral
surface.description: A clear walking or cycling surface in a stated material.
surface.designIdea: Connecting places and providing a legible route.

new_urbanism.label: New Urbanism
new_urbanism.description: Compact, connected neighbourhoods combining different uses and housing choices.
new_urbanism.designIdea: Walkable daily life and well-defined shared public space.
new_urbanism.componentLimit: A compatible frontage or street is one component; a whole-plan assessment is needed.

tod.label: Transit-oriented development
tod.description: Integrating land use with walking, cycling and useful public transport.
tod.designIdea: Access to activities with less dependence on cars.
tod.componentLimit: A station or tall building alone does not establish TOD, service quality or equitable outcomes.

garden_city.label: Garden City
garden_city.description: Combining settlement, landscape, local work and long-term community stewardship.
garden_city.designIdea: Healthy living and shared community benefit.
garden_city.componentLimit: Green space alone is not Garden City planning; land, governance, jobs and housing matter.

ecology.label: Green infrastructure
ecology.description: Treating water, habitat, planting and built development as related systems.
ecology.designIdea: Resilience and care for environmental processes.
ecology.componentLimit: Model appearance cannot establish stormwater capacity, biodiversity or carbon performance.

complete.label: Complete Streets
complete.description: Allocating street space for safe access by people using different modes and with different abilities.
complete.designIdea: Inclusive mobility and context-sensitive street design.
complete.componentLimit: A section alone does not verify crossings, speeds, networks or accessibility compliance.

auto.label: Car-oriented layouts
auto.description: Organising frontage, access or movement around motor vehicles and a hierarchy of roads.
auto.componentLimit: This describes a spatial priority, not the political beliefs of designers or users.

gsa.label: US General Services Administration: architectural styles

georgian.label: National Park Service: Georgian architecture at Independence Hall

newengland.label: Historic New England: architectural style guide

machiya.label: Kyoto Center for Community Collaboration: Kyo-machiya

second_empire.label: Parks Canada: Second Empire style in Canadian architecture

parkitecture.label: National Park Service: NPS Rustic / Parkitecture

cnu.label: Congress for the New Urbanism: Charter

complete.label: National Complete Streets Coalition: Complete Streets

garden_city.label: Town and Country Planning Association: Garden City Principles

vancouver.label: City of Vancouver: Vancouverism and planning

haussmann.label: City of Paris: Haussmann and the transformation of Paris

picturesque.label: National Park Service: Olmsted design principles

halifax.label: Canadian Register of Historic Places: Halifax Public Gardens

place.label: Project for Public Spaces: What is placemaking?

validation_timber_sanctuary_church_glaze.rationale: Glazed gable and exposed timber frames are explicitly described; local reference board is not hydrated for this audit.

validation_gothic_community_church_singl.rationale: Spire, rose window and vaulted nave establish Gothic-inspired design in the exact description; image was unavailable locally.

validation_reference_charcoal_gable_four.rationale: Four individual stoops and repeated steep gables suggest contemporary ground-oriented housing; no specific historical style is established.

validation_minimalist_infill_brick_monol.rationale: Restrained buff-brick volumes and deep precise openings support the minimalist classification.

validation_brewery_crystal_brewhouse.rationale: The faceted glass-and-steel brewhouse makes its frame and roof structure central to the image.

validation_museum_earth_sheltered.rationale: An earth-covered museum and projecting skylights merge architecture with the planted terrain; civic monumentality is not its style.

validation_clapboard_north_end.rationale: Reference shows a balanced clapboard facade with low roof; older variant text describes a gabled saltbox row. Maritime vernacular is the safe broad label.

validation_machiya_cafe_gallery.rationale: Timber lattice, deep traditional townhouse form and garden relationship support machiya; cafe reuse is a separate approach.

validation_cast_iron_italianate.rationale: Cast-iron columns, round arches and a strong cornice show an Italianate commercial facade.

validation_art_deco_streamline_moderne.rationale: Rounded corner glazing and continuous horizontal bands identify Streamline Moderne rather than a generic Deco tower.

validation_rndsqr_midrise_terraced_garde.rationale: Stepped planted terraces, warm cladding and a shop base support contemporary infill with biophilic features.

validation_rec_centre_timber_hall.rationale: An exposed timber gable and veranda give the community hall a contemporary timber and traditional shelter expression.

validation_contemporary_townhouse_timber.rationale: Vertical timber screens and a recessed ground-level entrance are legible in the townhouse reference.

native-park:botanical_garden_v3--native-.rationale: A conservatory and curated plant displays support botanical and gardenesque traditions; the building and garden have separate design vocabularies.

native-park:sculpture_garden_v0--native-.rationale: Art objects and viewing routes support a contemporary cultural court, without proving a named planning ideology.

native-park:student_neighbourhood_orchar.rationale: Fruit trees and shared outdoor space support productive-landscape principles; the clay reference does not establish ecological performance.

native-park:amphitheater_lawn_v0--native.rationale: Terraced landscape seating integrates performance into a planted lawn.

native-park:student_garden_square_v1--na.rationale: Timber, stone and gathering space support contemporary garden-square design; no historical garden school is established.

native-park:wetland_rain_garden_v0--nati.rationale: Wetland planting and water-edge boardwalks clearly support an ecological-landscape teaching theme.

amsterdam_gracht_v1.rationale: Canal banks, trees and an arched crossing establish a canal-city precedent; a specific transport hierarchy needs a network context.

brt_bus_rapid_transit_corridor_v0.rationale: Bus-priority corridor geometry supports transit-oriented components; station-area land uses and service are not established.

student_planted_shared_lane_v1.rationale: The authored shared lane combines planting and gathering; safe operation requires speed management and accessible navigation.

student_quiet_residential_street_v1.rationale: Walking routes and planting support walkable-neighbourhood principles; connected blocks cannot be inferred from one segment.

landmark_signature_bridge_v2.rationale: The current model is a landmark broad-deck bridge; exact architectural expression needs its local reference image.

validation_beltline_brick_modern.rationale: Brick bays, deep-set windows and ground-floor shops support contemporary contextual urban infill.

validation_infill_flat_roof_minimal.rationale: Flat roof, crisp volumes and large openings support minimalist contemporary infill.

native-park:research_garden_teaching_arb.rationale: Demonstration beds, plant displays and a teaching shelter support a productive educational landscape.

native-park:basketball_court_v1--native-.rationale: A court with seating and trees illustrates active neighbourhood public space; sport is a programme rather than a style.

validation_student_main_street_v1.rationale: Fine-grained shops, sidewalks, street trees and curbside parking support a traditional main-street component.

validation_student_market_street_v1.rationale: A pedestrian market street provides space for walking, stalls and gathering.

native-park:student_reading_garden_v2--n.rationale: Shade and quiet seating are documented; no locally hydrated image was available to establish a finer landscape tradition.

native-park:student_pickleball_garden_v1.rationale: Sport combined with social garden space supports recreation and public-life principles; fine aesthetic classification awaits image review.

native-park:student_tennis_garden_v2--na.rationale: A tennis court in planting is a garden recreation programme, not a distinct architectural movement.

native-park:student_bocce_garden_v2--nat.rationale: A pergola and social court suggest sheltered public recreation; Mediterranean authorship cannot be inferred from bocce alone.

native-park:urban_pocket_park_v0--native.rationale: The reference combines a curving path, planted refuge and timber shelter; the native and flexible choices retain distinct placement identities.

native-park:linear_park_greenway_v0--nat.rationale: A continuous path and meadow-like planting reference a reused railway corridor; adaptive reuse is an approach, not one aesthetic style.

native-park:inclusive_accessible_playgro.rationale: Woodland-themed inclusive play is documented; accessibility performance is not verified by the name.

clay_side_by_side_duplex.rationale: Two independent entrances and a shared narrow-lot composition make this a contemporary duplex, despite its parent's single-family use.

clay_montreal_plateau_duplex.rationale: Exterior stair, stacked homes and ornamental cornice identify a Montreal residential vernacular; duplex is its type.

clay_courtyard_brick_modern.rationale: A restrained brick entrance building and pedestrian passages support contemporary courtyard-housing vocabulary; the surrounding court is separately designed.

trial_postwar_bungalow.rationale: Ranch form is documented, but the present adjustable model and reference should be checked before teaching a strict historical-period example.

trial_edwardian_foursquare.rationale: Hipped roof, front dormer, square mass and columned porch identify the Edwardian Foursquare example with Classical influence.

clay_rammed_earth_infill.rationale: Rammed-earth walls, timber screens and shaded loggias are contemporary material expression, not sufficient evidence for a separate historical style.

clay_blue_glass_office_tower.rationale: A curtain-wall office shaft and glazed entrance are a contemporary continuation of glass-tower Modernism; its planning context is not established.

clay_vancouver_balcony_podium_tower.rationale: The narrow balcony tower, landscaped podium and lower shop wing illustrate Vancouverism's tower-and-podium component.

student_cycle_avenue_v1.rationale: Protected cycling space with pedestrian routes supports active-travel principles; continuity and junctions need separate review.

student_green_alley_v1.rationale: Community alley planting and social use support a ruelle-verte approach; ownership and community participation are not established by geometry.

student_school_street_v1.rationale: Playful paving and pedestrian space support a school-street teaching example; operations and access restrictions are not simulated.

native-park:student_woodland_stream_gard.rationale: Stream, stones, bridge and framed woodland views support Japanese inspiration, with no specific garden school established.

native-park:student_reflecting_fountain_.rationale: An axial paved court and water jets support contemporary formal composition; the current reference reads more paved than garden-like.

native-park:student_terraced_cafe_court_.rationale: Terraces and a centred fountain create a formal civic-space comparison; this alone is not a City Beautiful plan.

student_grass_tram_avenue_v1.rationale: Tram tracks, walking routes and planting are transit-priority components; grass tracks alone do not prove ecological benefit.

student_vine_pergola_promenade_v1.rationale: A shaded promenade supports pedestrian comfort and social use; a specific historical planning movement is not established.

student_grand_haussmann_boulevard_v1.rationale: The authored boulevard explicitly references Haussmann; frontage coordination and metropolitan layout remain wider-plan questions.

showcase_market.rationale: The iron-and-glass roof and brick market enclosure express a historic market-hall construction tradition.

showcase_aquatic.rationale: Expressed timber arches, glazed frontage and a planted roof support contemporary biophilic architectural intent.

showcase_tower.rationale: A setback crown, terracotta relief and vertical emphasis clearly support Art Deco.

autumn_timber.rationale: A timber structural grid, recessed balconies and roof planting justify the contemporary timber family; Nordic is a documented influence, not a location claim.

autumn_villa.rationale: Stone arcades, shutters and a tiled roof identify the Tuscan-inspired villa vocabulary.

autumn_cinema.rationale: Geometric relief, marquee and vertical blade sign identify the Art Deco cinema frontage.

native-park:student_urban_splash_plaza_v.rationale: Geometric paving and interactive water illustrate contemporary play-oriented public space.

native-park:student_stone_labyrinth_gard.rationale: Deliberate circular walking geometry supports a contemplative contemporary garden, not an automatic religious or historical attribution.

native-park:student_sheltered_dog_park_v.rationale: A fenced activity area and shelter support social recreation; no specific ideology follows from the programme.

student_london_cobbled_mews_v1.rationale: Narrow cobbled lane form references London's mews tradition; surface material does not prove low-speed or accessible operation.

student_cherry_blossom_street_v1.rationale: Cherry-tree planting adds a landscape identity; it does not establish a separate Japanese planning ideology.

student_barcelona_shaded_promenade_v1.rationale: A broad shaded walking space is Barcelona-inspired; this is not evidence of a Superblock or Cerdà grid.

clay_mass_timber_biophilic_barn.rationale: Exposed timber, a glazed reading hall and planted roof clearly support the proposed contemporary and biophilic tags.

clay_parisian_corner_cafe_culture.rationale: The rounded corner, mansard roof and cafe frontage support Parisian late-nineteenth-century eclecticism; an exact period attribution remains interpretive.

native-park:student_community_allotment_.rationale: Shared growing beds and a garden shelter support productive-landscape principles; governance and actual food yield are not established.

native-park:student_forest_adventure_v1-.rationale: Logs, planted edges and exploratory play support nature-play landscape design.

native-park:student_spiral_lookout_v1--n.rationale: A spiral lookout is documented; a more specific movement needs visual review of the unhydrated reference.

native-park:student_quarry_garden_v1--na.rationale: Quarry-inspired terrain supports a landscape-reclamation comparison; actual industrial reuse is not demonstrated.

native-park:student_cascade_water_garden.rationale: Cascading water is the documented organising feature; a precise historical garden style is not established.

clay_station_victorian_iron_glass.rationale: The large iron-and-glass train hall and historic masonry frontage belong to a Victorian engineering tradition; Victorian alone is a period label.

clay_biophilic_mass_timber_campus.rationale: Expressed timber bays, planting and a transparent teaching frontage justify biophilic contemporary timber architecture.

clay_mediterranean_resort_courtyard.rationale: Shaded loggias, stucco, tiled roof and courtyard support Mediterranean-inspired contemporary hotel design.

native-park:student_treetop_walk_v1--nat.rationale: Elevated canopy access suggests a landscape-led visitor experience; habitat and accessibility claims need evidence.

native-park:student_terraced_rose_v1--na.rationale: Roses and terraces establish a cultivated garden programme; no specific national formal-garden tradition is proven.

student_elevated_garden_rail_v1.rationale: Rail, walking, cycle route and planting form a multimodal corridor; the wider land-use strategy remains open.

skytrain_elevated_corridor_v0.rationale: Elevated railway and station hub are transit infrastructure; TOD requires surrounding access and land uses.

elevated_rail_transit_corridor_v0.rationale: A flowing canopy is documented; parametric is a form-generation description rather than a neighbourhood ideology.

native-park:student_sandy_beach_v1--nati.rationale: Sand, boardwalk and public activity support contemporary waterfront recreation.

native-park:student_prairie_picnic_grove.rationale: A prairie grove and picnic programme support a landscape-led public space; Prairie School is an unrelated architecture label.

native-park:student_neighbourhood_sports.rationale: A neighbourhood sports green is a recreation programme compatible with several urban approaches.

native-park:student_sensory_wellness_gar.rationale: Sensory planting and quiet relaxation support biophilic intent; health outcomes are not established.

native-park:student_bicycle_pump_track_p.rationale: Pump-track geometry is an activity design, not an architectural style or a complete cycling network.

native-park:student_urban_skate_plaza_v1.rationale: Skateable public space supports active public life; no particular planning movement follows from its name.

student_rain_garden_residential_street_v.rationale: Rain gardens and clear walking routes support green-street principles; hydrological performance remains unverified.

student_compact_one_way_shopping_street_.rationale: Compact shopping frontage and sidewalks support walkable-neighbourhood components; one-way operation alone has no ideological identity.

student_neighbourhood_cycle_street_v1.rationale: Dedicated walking and cycling space supports active travel; intersections and network connections need context.

student_separated_walking_cycling_greenw.rationale: Separate paths within planting establish an active-travel greenway rather than a specific architectural style.

student_neighbourhood_transit_stop_stree.rationale: Transit stop, sidewalks and planting support transit-access principles; a stop alone does not establish TOD.

native-park:court_only_basketball_v1--na.rationale: Markings, equipment and clear playing reserve are functional sports design; the surrounding park and planning approach are student decisions.

native-park:court_only_tennis_v1--native.rationale: Markings, equipment and clear playing reserve are functional sports design; the surrounding park and planning approach are student decisions.

native-park:court_only_pickleball_v1--na.rationale: Markings, equipment and clear playing reserve are functional sports design; the surrounding park and planning approach are student decisions.

native-park:court_only_beach_volleyball_.rationale: Markings, equipment and clear playing reserve are functional sports design; the surrounding park and planning approach are student decisions.

claude_trial_stepped_terraced_plaza_park.rationale: The park-only clay trial retains formal stepped paving; a full historical style cannot be established from this study.

claude_public_realm:cable-stayed-cycle-r.rationale: Exposed stay cables support a cycle ring; this is structural expression serving cycling connectivity.

claude_public_realm:calgary-riverwalk:22.rationale: Riverside walking space, seating and planting support a landscape-led public promenade.

claude_public_realm:halifax-public-garde.rationale: The named precedent is a Victorian public garden; this stripped model illustrates selected layout elements rather than the complete historic site.

claude_public_realm:ice-rink-market-squa.rationale: Seasonal rink and market uses support a flexible gathering-space approach; this is not a separate architectural movement.

claude_public_realm:inglewood-main-stree.rationale: Fine-grained brick shopfronts and pedestrian edges form a traditional commercial main street.

claude_public_realm:montreal-plateau-rue.rationale: Ground-oriented entrances and a fine-grained residential edge illustrate Montreal street-based urbanism.

claude_public_realm:princes-island-park:.rationale: The current reference is an urban planted terrace, so it should not be presented as a faithful stylistic account of the whole real island park.

claude_public_realm:rail-through-truss:d.rationale: Variant and current description say through-truss bridge, while the catalogue reference shows an arched masonry viaduct. Resolve the reference binding before teaching its structural type.

claude_public_realm:road-diet-complete-s.rationale: Reallocated road space, cycle provision and pedestrian edges are a direct Complete Streets teaching example; real safety is not certified.

claude_public_realm:steel-truss-road-bri.rationale: The exposed truss is the visual and structural organising feature; the bridge alone does not establish a car-oriented neighbourhood.

claude_public_realm:swooping-cycle-flyov.rationale: A sweeping elevated cycle route supports active travel with expressive civil structure.

claude_public_realm:weathering-steel-foo.rationale: A weathering-steel pedestrian truss supports a walking connection; material choice is separate from urban ideology.

clay_neoclassical_brick_headquarters.rationale: The symmetrical brick composition, Corinthian portico and dome directly support Neoclassical; office use does not imply a civic planning movement.

clay_admin_faculty_brick_bronze_fins.rationale: An ordered facade with bronze shading fins and a glazed entrance supports contemporary modernist influence.

clay_brick_timber_two_storey_office.rationale: Restrained brick wings frame an open court; courtyard is a type and spatial arrangement, not a style.

clay_strip_single_storey_classic.rationale: A low continuous canopy and repeated tenant bays form a utilitarian retail strip; Classic in the title does not mean Classical architecture.

clay_corten_timber_equipment_yard.rationale: Timber and weathering-steel screening enclose a service yard; a formally constituted architectural movement is not evident.

clay_meadow_three_gable_childcare.rationale: Repeated gables and a low timber veranda adapt familiar domestic forms for childcare.

clay_factory_sawtooth_roof.rationale: Repeated glazed sawtooth roof slopes, brick bays and working openings express a daylight-factory tradition.

clay_folded_roof_recovery_hall.rationale: A folded metal roof and large service enclosure support contemporary utilitarian design; waste programme alone does not prove ecological planning.

clay_garden_mews_six_homes.rationale: Small gabled homes with individual front doors face a shared court; the arrangement can support compact neighbourhood principles.

clay_horizon_double_section.rationale: A clerestory roof, broad glazing and low horizontal mass support contemporary modernist influence; manufactured is its construction method.

clay_industrial_gabled_metal_shed.rationale: Portal-frame enclosure, corrugated metal and gabled roof support industrial vernacular, not automatically Brutalism.

clay_industrial_tilt_up_concrete.rationale: Concrete panels and loading doors define a utilitarian industrial enclosure; tilt-up is a construction system.

clay_maple_porch_sage.rationale: A modest porch, horizontal siding and pitched roof give a new manufactured cottage traditional domestic expression.

clay_copperline_four_bay_depot.rationale: Four work bays and restrained cladding are a contemporary service-building expression rather than a precise historical movement.

clay_brick_timber_craftsman.rationale: Substantial porch supports, visible woodwork and the gabled cottage composition support Craftsman influence.

clay_prairie_cedar_chassis_home.rationale: Simple dark cladding, warm timber and a clear folded roof support the local Nordic-inspired tag; Prairie in the title does not establish Prairie School architecture.

clay_rndsqr_townhome_brick_contextual.rationale: Brick lower floors, articulated bays and individual street entries support contemporary contextual townhouses.

clay_warehouse_tilt_wall_mega.rationale: A large tilt-wall envelope and loading courts support logistics-oriented utilitarian design; its operations are vehicle dependent.

clay_ecole_republicaine_provincial_brick.rationale: The current reference is a restrained brick-and-stone school with clock element; it does not clearly show the historic polychrome and steep-roof variant text. Resolve identity before a precise style label.

clay_rndsqr_townhome_scandinavian_peaks.rationale: Alternating peaked roofs, pale walls and timber accents support the documented Nordic-inspired contemporary row.

clay_affordable_porchlight_original.rationale: Repeated pitched-roof townhouses and private street entrances are contemporary traditional-inspired ground housing; appearance cannot establish affordability.

clay_affordable_juniper_original.rationale: Small gabled cottages form a shared garden cluster; this supports compact-housing comparison, not a Garden City label by itself.

clay_affordable_stackyard_original.rationale: Exposed access gallery, external stairs and a simple two-level composition are contemporary stacked housing.

clay_affordable_aspen_original.rationale: A restrained brick apartment block uses an ordered window grid and shared entrance; no more specific historical style is established.

clay_affordable_switchback_original.rationale: A plain modular apartment composition uses repeated bays and material panels; modular construction is separate from architectural style.

community_brick_corner_grocery.rationale: The corner grocery and home above continue Montreal main-street vernacular; bracketed and arched details suggest Italianate influence without a firm historical attribution.

community_clerestory_neighbourhood_hall.rationale: Clear roof planes, clerestory glazing and expressed supports support civic Modernism influence.

community_inglewood_corner_merchants.rationale: Brick cornice, arched openings and upper shopfront composition read as traditional commercial architecture; the variant ID says Deco but does not establish visible Deco ornament.

community_log_recreation_cabin.rationale: Log walls, stone base and a sheltered porch support rustic recreation architecture with Parkitecture affinity.

community_prairie_neighbourhood_shops.rationale: A continuous pitched canopy and simple commercial bays form roadside retail vernacular, not Classical architecture.

final_seniors_apartments.rationale: Restrained brick, repeated recessed balconies and a garden terrace support contemporary residential design.

final_transit_pavilion.rationale: Exposed timber V-columns, a broad canopy and a transparent waiting hall make structure and public access legible.

final_courtyard_block.rationale: Homes over shops, a pedestrian passage and an open planted court support compact mixed-use urbanism.

final_health_centre.rationale: Timber shading frames, broad glazing and the garden-facing plan support contemporary civic design with biophilic intent.

final_urban_grocery.rationale: Roof lanterns reinterpret a daylight-factory form above a transparent neighbourhood grocery frontage.

claude_scottish_baronial_hotel.rationale: Crow-stepped gables, steep roofs and turrets identify this specific Scottish Baronial railway-hotel variant.

claude_parisian_corner_with_dome.rationale: Mansard roofs, dormers, corner dome and formal streetwall support Second Empire-influenced Parisian eclecticism; not every domed Parisian block is one pure style.

claude_grand_magasin.rationale: Ornate classical bays, a curved glass corner and roof dome support a Belle Epoque eclectic department-store identity.

claude_barcelona_mercat.rationale: Decorative entrance ironwork, coloured glass and repeated metal roof bays support Catalan Modernisme market architecture.

claude_montreal_second_empire_civic.rationale: A prominent clock tower, mansard roofs and dormers identify the Second Empire civic example; City Beautiful is only a possible composition comparison.

parkade_classic_concrete.rationale: The original elevation board shows an exposed structural grid and open decks; this is not enough to label the parkade Brutalist.

parkade_urban_brick.rationale: Brick piers and ventilation screens describe a contemporary contextual parkade, not a historic brick architectural movement.

parkade_green_terraces.rationale: Planted deck edges and climbing screens suggest biophilic intent while retaining the parking programme; planting does not erase vehicle priority.

parkade_solar_ribbon.rationale: Angled metal fins and a solar canopy suggest structural expression in a contemporary parkade; no carbon or energy performance is established.

parkade_mobility_courtyard.rationale: An open court, bicycle hub and street cafe create a mobility-hub comparison; the dominant programme remains vehicle storage.

claude_trial_arched_mill_mixed_use.rationale: Repetitive arched brick bays and a mill-conversion programme support historic industrial architecture with Italianate influence.

claude_trial_brick_podium_condo_tower.rationale: A balcony tower over a lower shop podium is compatible with tower-and-podium urbanism; location and planning authorship are not inferred.

claude_trial_calgary_cbe_brutalist_hq.rationale: Concrete massing, deep repetitive openings and strong projecting elements support Brutalism; its architecture alone does not establish a complete planning ideology.

claude_trial_campus_shed_office.rationale: Shed roof, exposed bracing and adapted work bays support an industrial reuse vocabulary; the same office parent also has a Neoclassical variant.

claude_trial_cmu_dock_warehouse.rationale: Plain block walls, raised docks and a service apron support utilitarian warehouse design; CMU is a material system, not Brutalism.

claude_trial_courtyard_primary_school.rationale: The variant description says Art Deco but the reference mainly shows plain flat-roofed masonry wings. Publish a broad modernist label only after checking the exact model's intended ornament.

claude_trial_ctrain_elevated_station.rationale: Current title and image show an elevated station, whereas legacy variant text describes an at-grade platform. Contemporary transit expression is plausible, but the exact teaching description needs reconciliation.

claude_trial_energy_centre.rationale: Glazed plant bays expose services within a brick frame; this supports contemporary industrial expression rather than automatic civic classicism.

claude_trial_garden_court_senior_residen.rationale: Tiled roofs, arcades and courtyard gardens suggest Mediterranean-inspired residential architecture; garden housing does not by itself establish Garden City governance.

claude_trial_gastown_heritage_commercial.rationale: Bracketed cornice, ornamental window heads and shopfront composition identify Italianate commercial architecture.

claude_trial_halifax_georgian_colonial.rationale: Balanced windows, central entrance and restrained hipped-roof composition support Georgian influence; current reference material differs from the older clapboard description.

claude_trial_halifax_waterfront_warehous.rationale: The reference shows an ornate arched-window commercial facade, while legacy text describes a gabled ironstone waterfront warehouse. Keep the exact style provisional until source identity is resolved.

claude_trial_led_grow_block.rationale: Repetitive dark panels and narrow LED-lit slots support contemporary utilitarian architecture; vertical farming is a use, not a style or ecological performance claim.

claude_trial_mews_coach_house.rationale: The stable opening, restrained upper windows and low roof support a Georgian-influenced mews conversion.

claude_trial_old_montreal_limestone_comm.rationale: The current reference and presentation describe a domed Classical-looking building; the variant ID and legacy text describe a steep-roofed French Colonial house. Do not teach either precise identity as settled.

claude_trial_plus15_glass_office_tower.rationale: Curtain wall and an elevated pedestrian bridge support contemporary glass-tower architecture; grade-separated walking is a planning comparison, not proof of pedestrian vitality or transit-oriented development.

claude_trial_slab_balcony_tower.rationale: Repetitive balcony slabs and a freestanding apartment shaft support mid-century Modernist influence; concrete alone does not make the example Brutalist.

claude_trial_toronto_bay_and_gable.rationale: Steep front gable, tracery-like bargeboard and projecting bay support a Victorian Gothic-influenced Toronto house type.

garden_gravel_path_v1.rationale: The authored path provides a material and walking connection; the material alone does not establish a historical or planning identity.

concrete_neighbourhood_walk_v1.rationale: The authored path provides a material and walking connection; the material alone does not establish a historical or planning identity.

brick_courtyard_path_v1.rationale: The authored path provides a material and walking connection; the material alone does not establish a historical or planning identity.

timber_garden_walk_v1.rationale: The authored path provides a material and walking connection; the material alone does not establish a historical or planning identity.

asphalt_shared_path_v1.rationale: A shared asphalt path supports walking and cycling connectivity; it is not a woonerf shared motor street.

standalone_narrow_sidewalk_v1.rationale: A standalone walking surface is a network component; width does not by itself certify accessible design or a planning movement.

standalone_neighbourhood_sidewalk_v1.rationale: A standalone walking surface is a network component; width does not by itself certify accessible design or a planning movement.

standalone_urban_sidewalk_v1.rationale: A standalone walking surface is a network component; width does not by itself certify accessible design or a planning movement.

flexible_pocket_park_v1.rationale: The reference combines a curving path, planted refuge and timber shelter; the native and flexible choices retain distinct placement identities.

flexible_linear_greenway_v1.rationale: A continuous path and meadow-like planting reference a reused railway corridor; adaptive reuse is an approach, not one aesthetic style.

flexible_shade_courtyard_v1.rationale: A restrained planted court and seating support contemporary neighbourhood public-space design.

flexible_meadow_grove_v1.rationale: Meadow textures and irregular planting support a naturalistic ecological aesthetic; actual species or habitat performance is unverified.

calgary_local_draft3_v1.rationale: The local road section assigns space to vehicle access and sidewalks; network design determines its wider walkability.

calgary_local_industrial_draft3_v1.rationale: A standard local industrial access section is an engineering and servicing component, not an aesthetic ideology.

calgary_collector_draft3_v1.rationale: Collector function and parking provision express road hierarchy; multimodal context requires separate assessment.

calgary_arterial_4lane_50_draft3_v1.rationale: Multiple traffic lanes and a large right-of-way support an automobile-oriented road-hierarchy comparison, independent of streetscape planting.

calgary_arterial_4lane_70_draft3_v1.rationale: Multiple traffic lanes and a large right-of-way support an automobile-oriented road-hierarchy comparison, independent of streetscape planting.

calgary_arterial_6lane_draft3_v1.rationale: Multiple traffic lanes and a large right-of-way support an automobile-oriented road-hierarchy comparison, independent of streetscape planting.

calgary_alley_draft3_v1.rationale: A service-access alley is compatible with several urban patterns; it is not automatically a shared social street.

calgary_local_high_activity_draft3_v1.rationale: The high-activity section offers an active-frontage comparison, but crossings, speeds and surrounding uses must support the claim.

calgary_collector_industrial_draft3_v1.rationale: Industrial collector geometry is primarily a servicing and vehicle-circulation section.

calgary_collector_high_activity_draft3_v.rationale: The high-activity section offers an active-frontage comparison, but crossings, speeds and surrounding uses must support the claim.

calgary_arterial_high_activity_draft3_v1.rationale: The high-activity section offers an active-frontage comparison, but crossings, speeds and surrounding uses must support the claim.

calgary_skeletal_draft3_v1.rationale: The broad skeletal road is a vehicle-hierarchy component; the model is a surface layout rather than a full engineered road profile.
